newsitem.title: UK: Brady bonds mixed as market awaits FOMC meeting.
newsitem.headline: Brady bonds mixed as market awaits FOMC meeting.

text.p: Brady bond prices were mixed in extremely thin trade on Monday as the market cautiously awaited the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Tuesday, emerging market experts said.
"The primary focus is the FOMC meeting," Neil Lockwood, emerging market analyst at ANZ Investment Bank in London said.
Uncertainty on whether the Federal Reserve would move to tighten monetary policy by 25 basis points continued to keep players sidelined, market analysts said.
According to a preliminary Reuters poll, experts were equally divided over whether the Fed would maintain current policy or hike rates by 25 basis points.

Though a 25 basis point increase in the Federal funds rate would likely lead to initial price declines in Brady debt instruments, market experts said prices should later rebound because the uncertainty of a Fed hike would be removed.

Richard Gray, emerging market analyst at BankAmerica in London, said: "We reckon they will tighten tommorrow, then we reckon there will be a brief blowout in spreads, but then the markets are a buy." "The markets will be stronger by the end of the week and heading upwards," Gray added.
Among Eastern European debt instruments, Russian Vnesheconombank dollar loans were 3/8 stronger at 84-7/8 bid and Bulgarian IABs were 1/8 firmer at 66-1/8 bid.
News that the International Monetary Fund agreed to resume lending to Russia and approved the release of almost $700 million helped boost Russian loan prices, market experts said.
In the Latin Brady market, prices were mixed but trading activity remained light.

"It is very quiet. I havn't seen a single trade go through this morning," said one Brady bond trader in London. Brazilian "C" bonds were 1/8 firmer at 76-1/8 as the allegations of cash-for-votes in Brazil continued to recede. Elsewhere, Argentine FRBs were unchanged at 92-3/8 bid and Mexican pars were 1/8 softer at 74-3/4 bid.
